profile.name: Rebecca
profile.review:
Rebecca is a 5-star Electro Pistols buffer who specializes in dealing Basic Attack damage and buffing Heavy Attacks. She has access to the Hack mechanic, a variant of Tune Rupture, and provides a secondary source of damage as well as Heavy Attack-related buffs to enhance your Main DPS’s firepower as much as possible.

Key Mechanics & Rotation

Rebecca has 2 states she can switch between freely in order to complete her rotations: Huntress and Guts. She swaps between them on every Intro and Skill cast, starting in Huntress state. Practically, she will use Guts state to generate most of her Forte gauge, trying to take advantage of its quick attacks throughout the majority of her rotaion, creating a loop since every rotation starts in Huntress state, switching to Guts upon a Skill use, leaving her in Huntress state for the start of every rotation (a state from which she will switch off quickly).

Each state brings small self-buffs to Rebecca, being 30% CRIT DMG and 15% DEF Ignore buffs, where she activates both at once upon casting Intro thanks to her automatically replenished Forte resource, Hot Hand.

Her manually replenished resource, called Fervor, is charged via her Intro, Dodge, Basic Attacks and Skill. When fully replenished, she casts a special Forte Heavy Attack, dealing a good amount of damage and restoring a lot of Concerto.

Rebecca’s Ultimate restores a ton of Concerto and deals a lot of damage as well. It occurs in 3 stages where Rebecca shoots 15 bullets total, progressively getting enhanced as the Basic Attack or Ultimate button is pressed every 5 shots (indicated on her Forte gauge). She then finishes off with a big blast of additional damage and Concerto that can be Swap-cancelled in optimal rotations. It also grants a small 20% ATK buff to the team upon casting.

Finally, her Outro amplifies All-type DMG and summons a turret that progressively increases the Heavy Attack DMG of the on-field character, the turret dealing constant damage as well. This totals up to 15% General Amplification and 35% Heavy Attack DMG Amplification, giving a maximum of 50% Amplification to Heavy Attackers when the full buffs are acquired  (this is instant for Lucy, but takes the full 14s for other characters).

Additionally, similarly to Lucy, Rebecca has access to a unique Tune Break response called Hack. It functions the same as Tune Rupture, just under a different name, but uses the same scalings and general mechanics otherwise, overall enhancing the damage of your Tune Break Skill casts when applied by several of Rebecca’s attacks.

As a result, Rebecca’s rotation will have her progressively work up towards her Forte Heavy Attack, followed by her Ultimate, and swapping out of her finisher attack (provided enough Concerto has been built ahead of time).

Meta Position & Conclusion

Rebecca deals good damage and has good Heavy Attack buffing potential. Functionally, in spite of a quite lengthy rotation at first glance, when optimized she is a straight upgrade to the already proven meta Heavy Attack buffer, being Mortefi (outside of some Mono Fusion teams with Lupa). As they are both free to acquire and have strong Heavy ATK buffing potential and a reliance on the same weapon and Echo set, being Static Mist and Moonlit Clouds, they fulfill the same niche, Rebecca overall performing a bit better thanks to a similar rotation speed, higher personal damage, and a better buffing profile. Disregarding different elements, which may give the advantage to one or the other depending on elemental resistance or Mono Fusion team compositions, Rebecca is generally slightly stronger in all Heavy Attack teams, with characters like Yangyang: Xuanling - Rebecca’s most important non-Lucy synergy that performs at top meta level -, Jingran, Jiyan, Augusta and Phoebe, especially considering when her Signature Weapon is acquired. Obviously, Rebecca is also used alongside Lucy, with whom she attains very solid performance although not meta-shaping.

In conclusion, for a free character, Rebecca is surprisingly very strong, being a “second Mortefi” of sorts who can strongly contribute to your Heavy Attack main damage dealers, having a particularly strong synergy with Yangyang: Xuanling, Lucy, and realistically all Heavy Attack-based teams in the game. She is strongly recommended to build if you have a valid use case for her on one of your Heavy Attack-based teams, as she works well even without her Signature weapon or extra Sequence nodes, making her accessible and generally quite strong!
profile.pros:
• Doesn’t need her Signature weapon to perform and easy to build Echoes-wise (good Energy generation);

  • Yet another Moonlit Clouds user, great to find new use in older character Echoes or build her from scratch without needing to spare many resources;

  • Fits into several teams beyond her intended DPS Lucy, can act as a stronger version of Mortefi (an already proven strong 4-star in the meta);

  • She’s free!
profile.cons:
• A lot of her attacks in her best loop rotations are prone to interruption, even if she’s supposed to benefit from Perfect Dodges, she often never ends up taking advantage of the mechanic; 

  • Collab character. If you don’t have her right now, you likely missed out forever, quite unfortunately.

profile.rotations:
Rotation & Gameplay

Rebecca’s rotation goal, similarly to Lucy, is to build towards her Forte Heavy Attack by quickly building her resource called Fervor. She can then build enough Concerto to use her Ultimate and swap its finisher attack at the end of her rotation. It’s possible to create a rotation where Rebecca can swap out of her Ultimate’s finisher attack on the first rotation, called “Boom! Fireworks”, by generating more Concerto than would be necessary. Due to the swap cancel, this will then carry over 10 Concerto Energy into the next rotation, for her to keep repeating this without needing to cast any extra attacks to build additional Concerto on any rotation that follows. This is Rebecca’s main optimization and a significant time save. This, however, means her first rotation looks different than any subsequent rotation, like so:

Echo Timing

Cancel Bell-Borne Geochelone/Impermanence Heron after the last Heavy Attack via her Ultimate.

Opener Rotation

  • Intro: Huntress 

  • Basic: Guts 1 (Cancel animation endlag via Dash)

  • Dash: Tactical Dodge

  • Basic: Guts 2

  • Basic: Guts 3

  • Heavy: Guts

  • Heavy (Forte): Guts

  • Heavy: Guts (Cancel animation endlag via Echo or Ultimate)

  • Ultimate

  • Boom! Fireworks (Cast automatically) (Swap)

  • Outro

This saves 1.43s on the Boom! Fireworks swap by extending the rotation for about 1.09s of extra rotation time spent casting Guts Basics, netting a 0.34s time save on the first rotation, and the full 1.43s on any following rotation, making this “extended” Opener always worth it.

Now that we can carry over 10 Concerto from our Opener Rotation into our Loop, we are free to swap cancel Boom! Fireworks without the need for extra attacks. We also have a bit of Fervor built up from our previous rotation. This allows us to do the following:

Loop Rotation

  • Intro: Huntress (Cancel animation endlag via Jump)

  • Jump

  • Basic: Plunging Attack (Cancel animation endlag via Skill)

  • Skill (Switch to Guts form) (Cancel animation endlag via Dash)

  • Dash: Tactical Dodge

  • Basic: Guts 2

  • Heavy (Forte): Guts 

  • Heavy: Guts (Cancel animation endlag via Echo/Ultimate)

  • Ultimate

  • Boom! Fireworks (Cast automatically) (Swap)

  • Outro

Additional Tips & Tricks

On the final rotation, Rebecca can skip the last Heavy: Guts executed in her loop rotation, as it is not performed for Concerto generation, but for Fervor generation. However, if Rebecca won’t rotate another time, this additional Fervor is not needed and can be skipped. This saves approximately a second of rotation time.

In Quickswap, Rebecca makes frequent use of her Guts Heavy Attack, as it constitutes her best Swap Cancel window. However, note she may not use quickswap until her Intro has been cast, as it is a big source of Fervor generation, and Hot Hand must be full before casting it for it to grant any Fervor. 1 Intro, 1 Skill, 3 Heavies and a Basic Attack are enough to fill her Fervor gauge, so fit these attacks into your Quickswap rotation accordingly if you wish to use Rebecca in Quickswap.

skills.name: Mix-'n'-Match
skills.description:
Basic Attack - Huntress

  • Perform up to 3 consecutive attacks, dealing Electro DMG.

Heavy Attack - Huntress

  • Hold Normal Attack to continuously fire at enemies at the cost of STA, dealing Electro DMG, considered Basic Attack DMG.

    • Hold and then release Normal Attack while Rebecca is not casting Tactical Dodge - Huntress to cast Heavy Attack - Eat Lead!: Huntress

Heavy Attack - Eat Lead!: Huntress

  • Deal Electro DMG.

Comin' in Hot! - Huntress

  • Somersault in mid-air and land.

  • Keep holding Normal Attack after casting this skill to follow up with Heavy Attack - Huntress without consuming STA.

Mid-air Plunging Attack - Huntress

  • Consume STA to perform a Plunging Attack, dealing Electro DMG.

Dodge Counter - Huntress

  • Press Normal Attack shortly after a successful Dodge to strike the target, dealing Electro DMG.

Tactical Dodge - Huntress

  • Press Dodge to attack the target while dodging, dealing Electro DMG.

  • Can be cast during the following actions (while on the ground):

    • Performing Basic Attack - Huntress.

    • Performing Heavy Attack - Huntress.

    • Performing Heavy Attack - Eat Lead!: Huntress

    • Casting Comin' in Hot! - Huntress.

    • Casting Tactical Dodge - Huntress.

    • Casting Resonance Skill.

    • Casting Intro Skill.

  • Additional Electro DMG is dealt upon a successful Dodge during Tactical Dodge - Huntress.

  • Keep holding Normal Attack after casting this skill to follow up with Heavy Attack - Huntress without consuming STA.

Basic Attack - Guts

  • Perform up to 3 consecutive attacks, dealing Electro DMG.

  • Casting Tactical Dodge - Guts does not reset Basic Attack - Huntress's attack cycle within a certain time.

Heavy Attack - Guts

  • Consume STA and attack the target, dealing Electro DMG.

Mid-air Plunging Attack - Guts

  • Consume STA to perform a Plunging Attack, dealing Electro DMG.

Dodge Counter - Guts

  • Press Normal Attack shortly after a successful Dodge to strike the target, dealing Electro DMG.

Tactical Dodge - Guts

  • Press Dodge and attack the target while dodging, dealing Electro DMG.

  • Can be cast during the following actions (while on the ground):

    • Performing Basic Attack - Guts.

    • Casting Tactical Dodge - Guts.

    • Casting Resonance Skill.

    • Casting Intro Skill.

skills.name: Party 'til Dawn!
skills.description:
Switching to Mk. 31 HMG mode generates a field of Stagnation for 9.5s, in which:

Rebecca fires the Mk. 31 HMG automatically, dealing Electro DMG, considered Basic Attack DMG, while accumulating Overload. Press or hold Normal Attack or press Resonance Liberation at intervals after Rebecca starts firing to enhance her Mk. 31 HMG's firepower and accumulate Overload faster. This effect can be triggered up to 2 times.

  • The machine gun will only auto-lock onto the enemy closest to the crosshair in the aim down sight.

  • Rebecca is immobile when firing the Mk. 31 HMG and gains 50% DMG Reduction and Immunity to Interrruption.

Overload

  • Rebecca can hold up to 90 points of Overload.

  • Hitting targets with the standard firepower Mk. 31 HMG grants 2 points.

  • Hitting targets with the enhanced firepower Mk. 31 HMG grants 4 points.

  • Hitting targets with the twice-enhanced firepower Mk. 31 HMG grants 6 points.

BOOM! Fireworks!

  • After Mk. 31 HMG mode ends or when Overload is maxed, BOOM! Fireworks! is automatically cast, dealing Electro DMG. Casting BOOM! Fireworks! ends Mk. 31 HMG.

    • Hold Resonance Liberation while in Mk. 31 HMG mode to immediatly cast BOOM! Fireworks!.

    • Leaving the Mk. 31 HMG mode removes all Overload.

skills.name: Gloves Are Comin' Off!
skills.description:
Switch Gears!

  • Upon casting Resonance Skill or Intro Skill, Rebecca can freely switch between the Huntress and Guts modes.

    • The Huntress mode increases Rebecca's Crit. DMG by 30%.

    • The Guts mode allows Rebecca to ignore 15% of the target's DEF.

  • By default, Rebecca starts in the Huntress mode.

Hack - Shifting

  • Rebecca inflicts Hack - Shifting upon dealing damage to the targets through the following skills. The same skill can trigger this effect once every 3s:

    • Intro Skill - Yo, It's Big Boomin' Time!, Intro Skill - Hey, Leadhead, Come 'n' Get Me!, Heavy Attack - Rat-tat-tat!: Huntress, Heavy Attack - Bang-bang-bang!: Guts, and Resonance Liberation - BOOM! Fireworks!.

Hack Response - Meltdown

  • Deal Electro DMG to all targets affected by Hack - Interfered within the range, considered Hack DMG.

Heavy Attack - Rat-tat-tat!: Huntress

  • At 120 points of Fervor, Heavy Attack - Huntress is replaced with Heavy Attack - Rat-tat-tat!: Huntress. Hold Normal Attack to cast Heavy Attack - Rat-tat-tat!: Huntress, which consumes all Fervor to pull in nearby targets and deal Electro DMG, considered Basic Attack DMG.

  • During Heavy Attack - Huntress, if Fervor is at 120 points and Rebecca is not in the action of Tactical Dodge - Huntress, release Normal Attack to cast Heavy Attack - Rat-tat-tat!: Huntress.

Heavy Attack - Bang-bang-bang!: Guts

  • At 120 points of Fervor, Heavy Attack - Guts is replaced with Heavy Attack - Bang-bang-bang!: Guts. Hold Normal Attack to cast Heavy Attack - Bang-bang-bang!: Guts, which consumes all Fervor to pull in nearby targets and deal Electro DMG, considered Basic Attack DMG.

Fervor

  • Rebecca can hold up to 120 points of Fervor.

  • Normal Attacks restore Fervor upon damaging the target.

  • Resonance Skill restores Fervor upon damaging the target.

  • When A Girl Gets What She Wants! is gained by casting Intro Skill - Yo, It's Big Boomin' Time! or Intro Skill - Hey, Leadhead, Come 'n' Get Me!, Rebecca restores 50 points of Fervor.

Hot Hand

  • Rebecca can hold up to 120 points of Hot Hand.

  • Regenerates over time at a rate of 10 points per second.

  • Casting Heavy Attack - Rat-tat-tat!: Huntress or Heavy Attack - Bang-bang-bang!: Guts restores 40 points.

A Girl Gets What She Wants!

  • At 120 points of Hot Hand, casting Intro Skill - Yo, It's Big Boomin' Time!, Intro Skill - Hey, Leadhead, Come 'n' Get Me!, Resonance Skill - It's Big Boomin' Time!, or Resonance Skill - Come 'n' Get Me! grants the following effects for 12s:

    • Rebecca simultaneously gains the Stat Bonuses of both the Huntress and Guts modes, regardless of which mode she's currently in.

Hot Hand cannot be restored during this period and is consumed by 10 points per second.

weapons.Comment: Rebecca's Signature is of course her best in slot, as it can boost party-wide ATK more significantly than its permanent counterpart Static Mist, while giving Rebecca higher damaging stats with its Basic DMG and CRIT DMG bonuses.

Lynae's Signature provides Rebecca with a constant Basic DMG Bonus self-buff as well as significant ATK and CRIT Rate bonuses. While it doesn't offer the team-wide DMG Bonus buff as Rebecca can't apply Tune Rupture, it comes out on top of other options below it by sheer personal damage increase alone, making it a very strong alternative to her Signature.

Best permanent option when privileging Team DPS. While this weapon offers lower personal damage than a lot of others below it, the ATK% buff it offers to the next incoming character via Outro makes it a very strong weapon for any Pistols 2nd slot buffer, and Rebecca is no exception, as this weapon constitutes a perfect permanent option and alternative to her Signature.

This weapon hones in on Rebecca's personal damage more than Static Mist, and it sacrifices team DPS to increase her own damage instead. Generally, this trade-off is not worth it in a full team context, but it's almost as good as Static Mist still and a good alternative to her Signature as well.
Simple ATK and CRIT Rate stat-stick for Rebecca, who does not benefit from this weapon's Aero Erosion-related effects.
Simple ATK and CRIT DMG stat-stick for Rebecca, who barely benefits from this weapon's Skill DMG-related effects.
Simple ATK and CRIT DMG stat-stick for Rebecca, who does not benefit from this weapon's Spectro and Heavy DMG-related effects.
Simple ATK and CRIT DMG stat-stick for Rebecca, who does not benefit from this weapon's Heavy and Echo DMG-related effects.
This Battle Pass exclusive is the best 4-star choice Rebecca has access to, it grants her with some ATK and CRIT Rate but falls behind any 5-star significantly due to a low Base ATK.
Best no-gacha option if necessary, granting some extra ATK when no damage is taken by the character equipping it. Upgrade to 5-star options as soon as possible though.

echoes.Comment: This set sacrifices Rebecca's personal damage in order to provide higher buffing to a single character. It provides an extra 10% Energy Regen to the wielder unconditionally and gives 22.5% ATK to the incoming character for 15s after casting Outro skill.
echoes.Echo_1_Comment: Provides 10% DMG Bonus for 15s as well as DMG reduction for 3 hits. If hit 3 times, the damage buff runs out, which means you want to avoid getting hit to make full use of this Echo; however, it's optimal on Rebecca as it can be cast right before her Ultimate (after her Forte Heavy Attack) in order to cancel the animation, buff your main DPS, the most of Rebecca's rotation, as well as the most of your Support's rotation (just make sure to frontload their damage if possible/needed).
echoes.Echo_2_Comment: Niche Main Echo for specifically the Jingran/Rebecca/Verina team. Should be used during Verina's rotation before Rebecca Intros in, provides a Shield to Jingran in order for him to gain a lot of Fusion DMG Bonus.

echoes.Set_small_2: Endless Resonance, Reel of Spliced Memories
echoes.Set_small_3: Moonlit Clouds, Empyrean Anthem, Tidebreaking Courage
echoes.Comment: Grants Rebecca an easily activated Basic and Heavy DMG Bonus increase. This is a 1-piece set with only 1 Main Echo possible that also grants Rebecca additional CRIT Rate, making it the overall best blend of stats she can have for her personal damage (sacrificing team buffing in the process), paired alongside 2 2-piece sets. These sets include:
echoes.Echo_1_Comment: Only Echo for the Shadow of Shattered Dreams set, simple summon Echo that grants an extra 15% CRIT Rate to Lucy or Rebecca.

echoes.Comment: Lynae's Signature Echo set can be utilized by Rebecca (in Lucy's team specifically) which can grant a higher total set of buffs than what Moonlit Clouds provides. However, due to the inability of this Echo set to increase Rebecca and her Support's damage as well (possible with Bell-Borne Geochelone main Echo), it is a very close contender but not a stronger one than Moonlit Clouds, with lower overall usability in non-Lucy teams. It is still a close contender if you have the Echoes and don't want to farm a separate Moonlit set for Rebecca though.
echoes.Echo_1_Comment: Simple summon Echo with the special property of giving an extra 10% DMG Bonus to the next character switched into via an Outro. Sacrifices small amounts of personal damage usually seen in Main Echoes for extra damage increase to the DPS, which is highly preferred by buff-focused characters.

teams.Comments: Shorekeeper may prove stronger in Whimpering Wastes as building Off-Tune multiple times on the same enemy (the reason why Mornye is ran) will almost never happen in that gamemode.

synergies.Comment: Yangyang, Xuanling is the highest Heavy Attack damage dealer in the game. It's no surprise that Rebecca's best team is alongside her as she is her best Heavy Attack DMG buffer, on par with the generalist top tier Lynae. Finally, while Rebecca can detach from Lucy, Lucy definitely can't detach from Rebecca; both characters are capable of increasing each other's damage substantially and interact together via the Hack mechanic, making it Rebecca's second best pairing.

Rebecca can also pair successfully with a wide variety of Heavy Attack damage dealers, being akin to a second Mortefi of sorts. Thanks to her solid personal damage and ability to buff Heavy Attacks via her Outro, she fits nicely for all Heavy damage dealers listed prior as a capable buffer.

Rebecca can use a variety of generalist Supports for her team's third slot. Mornye is ideal for the team with Lucy to put the highest possible emphasis on Hack damage via her ability to buff the team's Off-Tune Buildup Rate. In other teams however (or simply in Whimpering Wastes where building off-tune multiple times on the same enemy will almost never happen), Shorekeeper may prove a stronger alternative due to her ability to buff the team's CRIT Rate and DMG, while Verina is the old reliable alternative to Shorekeeper with lower buffs but always being accessible on the permanent banner.
